h1: What Is a Project Baseline? Scope, Schedule and Cost
seo_title: What Is a Project Baseline? Scope, Schedule and Cost
meta_description: What a project baseline is, the scope, schedule and cost baselines, how reserves fit, how to set and re-baseline, with a worked example and BEI check.
excerpt: A project baseline is the approved scope, schedule or cost plan you measure performance against. This guide covers the three baselines and the PMB, reserves, how to set a baseline, legitimate re-baselining, a calculated worked example with BEI, and Agile and PRINCE2 equivalents.
learning_objectives: Define a project baseline and distinguish it from the current plan, forecast and target
Describe the scope, schedule and cost baselines and the performance measurement baseline
Explain how contingency and management reserve relate to the cost baseline and project budget
Set a baseline using clear entry criteria
Calculate SV, CV, SPI, CPI and BEI against a baseline and interpret them
Distinguish legitimate baseline changes from performance events and keep a versioned baseline log

formulas.formula: EMV = P × I; contingency = sum of EMVs
Cost baseline = work package budgets + contingency; project budget = cost baseline + management reserve
SV = EV − PV; CV = EV − AC; SPI = EV/PV; CPI = EV/AC; SV% = SV/PV×100; CV% = CV/EV×100
formulas.variables: PV, EV, AC in £k; indices unitless

formulas.formula: BEI = baseline tasks with actual finish ÷ baseline tasks scheduled to finish by status date
